hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens allowed on a residential lot with no permit, provided the coop is in the rear yard at least 20 ft from any dwelling; more (up to 10, then up to 20) are allowed with a permit and greater distance from dwellings.
permit_notes: No permit needed for 6 or fewer hens. Keeping more requires a permit from the city, with the allowed count rising as distance from neighboring dwellings increases.
setback_notes: Coop must be in the rear yard and at least 20 ft from any dwelling unit, not just a property line; placement in the front yard or a side setback area is not allowed.
coop_rules: Coop must be in the rear yard; general sanitation and nuisance provisions apply under Title 7 (Animal Care and Control).
zoning_notes: Rules apply to residential zoning; roosters are not allowed in any residentially zoned area.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: San Jose Municipal Code, Title 7 Animals (PDF)
Urban Chickens Network, San Jose CA
